edges.description: Sperm without a flagellum cannot move.
Immotile sperm cannot reach or fertilize the oocyte in vivo.
The knockout reproduces the predominantly flagellum-less sperm seen in patients.
Sperm number falls in both species, but more steeply in the mouse.
edges.limitations: Only very few sperm can be recovered from knockout epididymides, while patients still have about 1-21 million sperm per ejaculate. The mouse spermatogenic defect is more severe than in the two reported men. Mouse sperm also show residual cytoplasm and abnormal heads, which were not described in patients.

nodes.description: The sperm flagellum grows from the distal centriole, which must mature into a basal body and dock at the membrane. Patient sperm have abnormal centriole numbers and orientation (no centrin dot, or more than two), and IFT88 and IFT140 are mislocalized to the head and neck and absent from the tail. The authors attribute both the flagellar failure and the centriole disorder to centrosomal damage from DZIP1 loss.

nodes.description: A CRISPR frameshift in exon 2 removes DZIP1 protein from the testis. Homozygous males are infertile, with very few epididymal sperm, no motile sperm, and mostly absent flagella. DZIP1 is normally expressed in germ cells, especially elongated spermatids.
Sperm are essentially immotile: total motility 0-2.1% and progressive motility 0% across two semen analyses in each proband.

nodes.description: The missense variant p.Arg63Gln lowers DZIP1 levels and the stop-gain p.Tyr230* removes the three coiled-coil domains. DZIP1 is undetectable in patient sperm, where it normally concentrates in the head and neck, the region that holds the sperm centrioles. DZIP1 is an adaptor at the mother centriole: it binds the appendage protein CEP164 and the IFT component IFT88, and it assembles the BBSome-DZIP1-PCM1 complex at centriolar satellites.
